guide.title: Assisted Ventilation
guide.lead: If breathing is absent or inadequate, you breathe for the patient. Get a good seal, give small breaths at a slow rate, and stop each one when the chest rises. Faster and harder breaths make things worse, not better.

sections.title: The numbers
notes: Adult volume is about 500–600 mL (6–7 mL/kg): just enough to see the chest rise.
Oxygen at 15 L/min with the reservoir attached.

steps.title: Open and hold
steps.text: Head-tilt/chin-lift or jaw thrust; OPA or NPA.

steps.title: Seal with two people
steps.text: One holds the mask with both hands (E-C clamp), the other squeezes. Far better than one rescuer.

steps.title: Squeeze gently
steps.text: Over about 1 second, stop at chest rise, let it fall.

steps.title: Watch
steps.text: Chest rise, SpO₂, colour, gastric distension.

sections.title: Troubleshooting
rows: Too fast or too much volume
High pressure in the chest reduces venous return
notes: Routine cricoid pressure is not recommended.

quiz.q: Why can over-ventilation drop blood pressure?
options: Raised pressure in the chest reduces venous return
quiz.explanation: Less blood returns to the heart.

First thing to check when the chest won't rise despite a good seal:
options: Head position and obstruction; suction if needed

flashcards.question: Infant or child ventilation rate (with a pulse)
BVM breath volume
flashcards.answer: Just enough for visible chest rise (adult about 500–600 mL).

flashcards.question: Why two-rescuer BVM?
flashcards.answer: Both hands seal the mask (E-C clamp) while the other person squeezes.

flashcards.question: Gastric distension
flashcards.answer: From ventilating too fast or with too much volume: slow down, smaller breaths.

flashcards.question: Commonest cause of poor chest rise
flashcards.answer: A poor mask seal: two-rescuer technique and reposition.

flashcards.question: Near-100% oxygen with a BVM
flashcards.answer: Oxygen at 15 L/min with the reservoir attached.

critical.scenario: You are ventilating an apneic adult at about 30 breaths per minute. The pulse begins to weaken.
critical.question: What's wrong?

options.t: Too fast: slow to 1 breath every 6 seconds
Give fluids and keep the rate

critical.kpi: Ventilates at the correct rate to preserve circulation

critical.scenario: During one-rescuer BVM you can't keep a seal, and the abdomen is distending.
critical.question: Two most important corrections?

options.t: Two-rescuer BVM for a better seal; smaller, slower breaths

critical.kpi: Optimizes BVM seal and avoids gastric insufflation

critical.scenario: An OPA is in place, but the chest doesn't rise despite a good two-hand seal.
critical.question: Next?

options.t: Reposition the head and airway, check for obstruction, suction if needed

critical.scenario: A 4-year-old with a pulse has slow, gasping breaths after a seizure.
critical.question: Ventilation rate?
critical.kpi: Ventilates a child with a pulse at 1 breath every 2–3 seconds
